You are not Christ’s disciples / but those of the Antichrist / of the Whore of Babylon <note>A biblical reference used here to criticize the perceived corruption of the institutional church</note>: No priest is capable of his office / unless he is in God's Will: His granting of absolution is no absolution at all / rather, the community of Christ absolves him / to whom he surrenders himself: He is of as much use to the Church / as a fifth wheel is to a wagon: You Sophist / how do you wish to share the <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> <note>original: "Great Mystery"; for Böhme, this is the hidden source of all being and the manifestation of God’s wisdom</note> / which you do not possess? The community has it / and the repentant sinner who comes to you / they have it / and you are a Sophist: You would be better off in a cowshed / than in the Church: How could the Devil absolve a repentant person? And you serve only your idol-belly <note>original: "Abgott-Bauch"; a reference to those who serve their own physical appetites and greed rather than God</note>.

54. Oh, you blind world / how you are blinded / you believe / that you must not touch the <term>Mysterium Magnum</term> / that you are not worthy of it / and that the priest alone is worthy of it: If you are in Christ / then you have everything freely / you have his covenant with Baptism and the Sacrament / and the Body and Blood

<meta>Christ's</meta>

<summary>Böhme critiques the institutional clergy, arguing that spiritual authority and the "Mysterium Magnum" belong to all true believers in Christ rather than being a commodity to be sold or controlled by "Sophists." <meta>This page continues Böhme's discourse on the true nature of the church. Having previously criticized the "Sophists" (scholarly theologians) for gatekeeping the divine, he now moves to distinguish between the physical institution of the church and the spiritual "living temple" found within the believer. He argues that the sacraments and the presence of God are not confined to buildings but exist wherever the community of believers gathers.</meta>

# Chapter 11. Of Man.

...of Christ therein: For the covenant belongs to the believers, and not to the **Sophists** <term>Sophists: Böhme's derogatory term for academic theologians who prioritize intellectual logic over spiritual experience</term>. After all, Christ’s disciples, and then their own disciples and successors, baptized; and the believing **community** <term>Gemeine: The spiritual fellowship or congregation of believers</term> broke the bread of Christ in houses, and wherever they were able, and partook of the body and blood of Christ. The **Temple of God** was everywhere that Christians were gathered together.

55. We do not report such things to tear down the churches in which one carries out Christ’s office, but rather we show you the hypocrites who bind you to themselves, so that you may go out from them to the community of Christ. Go into the community of Christ, and go into the temple of Christ, and do not let yourselves be satisfied merely with the **stone-walled churches** <term>Mawer-Kirchen: Literally "wall-churches," referring to physical, institutional buildings which Böhme considers spiritually "dead" if they lack the living Spirit</term>, for such a church is a heap of stones and is dead, but Christ’s temple is living. You all make your peace with the institutional church and enter into it, but into the temple of Christ no one wants to go. Go into the temple of Christ, so shall you become living from out of death. There is no other counsel, neither in heaven nor in this world; it must be so, or else you remain in darkness.

56. We do not judge so harshly: For God’s will stands open to all people, let them be called by whatever name they wish. Chapter 11.

57. We say that in all **opinions** there is heresy and the **Antichrist**. You have Christ with His Word; cling simply to it—not to the **letter** alone, but to the **living Word**, which is God and man. This is the Scripture that you should read and preach out of Christ’s Spirit, and not out of mere fancy. But if you are incapable of that, why then do you teach so much and devise opinions? Do you think God is a **liar** like you, that He would take your fabricated opinion for His Word, when you are yet dead to God? He who merely "opines" whether a thing be so or not, doubts. Now, doubt is no faith, but rather a path that is dangerous to walk.

58. Run after me! That other one is a **heretic** and speaks from a false spirit!" To which party should I then turn? Where should I go so that I may hear the true **Gospel** preached?

...how shall we then speak of him? If we wish to speak of him rightly, we must speak from out of his Spirit, for that witnessed of God. But if we speak out of **skill** <term>Kunst: human-learned art, science, or technical skill</term> and **histories** <note>Referring to external historical accounts or traditional doctrines without internal spiritual experience</note>, then we speak out of ourselves and not out of God, and we are murderers and thieves, and not the **shepherds of Christ** <note>original: "Christi Hirten"</note>.

A thief comes only to steal and to rob: Likewise, the **squabblers** <term>Zäncker: those who engage in religious disputes and theological fighting</term> come in their own name, desiring to have a great reputation and to possess rich **benefices** <term>Pfründen: ecclesiastical livings or land-based incomes for clergy</term> or **prebends** <term>Præbenden: stipends or payments granted to members of a church</term>. 65. Dear children of Christ, stop your ears against the **vicious wolves** <term>Laster-Wölffen: literally "vice-wolves" or "slanderous wolves"</term>, for they do not only bring shame upon one another, but upon the **congregation of Christ** <note>original: "Gemeyne Christi"</note>, which is everywhere in all lands where there are **penitent people** <term>bußfertige Menschen: those who are truly repentant and humble before God</term>. Those who regret their sins, depart from them, and turn themselves toward the mercy of God—those are in Christ, even if they are **Turks** <note>original: "Türcken"—in Böhme's time, this term was a general label for Muslims or non-Christian people of the Ottoman Empire</note>. 71. **Open your eyes**, you children of Christ! This is the **Antichrist**; do not follow after him. Many a person has been a sinner, yet has turned away from his sins and entered into Christ; such a soul is an angel of God in Christ. Why do you, you proud **Adversary** <note>original: "Wiederchrist," meaning one who stands against Christ</note>, dare to mock the angels of God out of your own selfish desires? You blind man, do you not see? If you are Christ’s shepherd and servant, and God’s vicar <term>Statthalter: a representative or deputy acting in God’s place</term>, and if you have the **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterium Magnum: the hidden spiritual essence or "great secret" of God's creation</term> with you—if your office is truly Christ’s office, as you boast—why then are you a liar? You praise the ungodly for the sake of money; did Christ and his **Apostles** ever do such a thing?

72. Listen, you Adversary: Look at the **Acts of the Apostles** <note>referring to the story of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5</note>, where a man sold his possessions and laid a portion of the money at the Apostles’ feet. Peter asked him: "Did you sell the field for such a price?" And when he said "yes"—yet held a false and doubting mind—Peter said: "You have lied to the **Holy Spirit**. Look, the feet [of those who will carry you out] are at the door to carry you away from the **Community of Truth**." What do you think of yourself now? If this judgment befell a layman and a listener of Peter, what would have happened to St. Peter himself if he had chased after money with lies and blasphemed the Holy Spirit in such a way? But you do exactly this: you praise an unrighteous man just so that you may obtain money, caring nothing for his soul. You also care nothing that you pour your lies into the **Community of Christ**. How many a person stands there and often sighs over his own falsehood and deceit...

# Of the Threefold Life Ch. 11.

...[if] we find ourselves, then we find everything; we need not run anywhere to seek God, and in this way, we can do him no service: If we only seek and love one another, then we love God: What we do to one another, we do to God: Whoever seeks and finds his brother and sister has sought and found God: We are all in him one body in many members, where each has his task, his governance and doing, and that is God’s wonder: We were known in his <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: *Weißheit*. ## Chapter 12.

### On the Christian Life and Conduct: What man must do in this valley of misery so that he may perform **GOD's** work and thus attain the eternal, highest good.

1. For man in this valley of misery <note>original: "Jammerthal." A common biblical and mystical metaphor for the earthly world of suffering.</note> on earth, nothing is more necessary and useful than that he learn to know himself: what he is, where he is from, and where he wants to go; what he strives for, and where he travels when he dies. This is the most useful thing for everyone to know: for the outward conduct <term>conduct (Wandel): the way one lives and behaves in the physical world</term> remains in this world, but whatever the heart grasps, man takes with him.

2. The will of the soul-spirit <note>original: "Seelen-Geist." The author’s term for the inner, spiritual aspect of the soul that connects to the divine.</note> is eternal; whatever is encompassed within the will of the soul-spirit, the soul takes with it when body and soul part. Therefore, it is necessary for us to strive for something good, in which the soul can spend its eternal play and in which it may have its joy; for our soul-works follow us—

We will tell her of the great tribulations that we had in Jericho <note>Jericho is used here as a symbol for the fallen, material world of strife and spiritual distance from God.</note>: We will speak of the great danger when we were among many evil beasts; we will speak of the driver <term>Treiber: a taskmaster or oppressor, often representing the devil or the harsh spirit of the worldly law</term> who held us captive so long, and speak of how we became free of him: Let us be one, so that our Mother may not be troubled and have a loathing for us.

12. Thus, and in no other way, is the teaching of Moses and all the prophets: that we should love one another as one life, and God in us. But behold, what has the Antichristian Devil sown into this? He has sown <term>pride</term><note>original: "Hoffart." A term frequently used by Böhme to describe the arrogant haughtiness and spiritual vanity that leads to the fall.</note> and lies, honor with power and splendor. He has installed himself upon the seat of Moses and the prophets, as well as into the authority of Christ, and has led us astray so that we have separated from one another. He has raised up the issue of <term>election</term><note>original: "Wahl." Böhme is critiquing the theological debates over predestination (the "choice" of who is saved), which he believed caused division and malice among Christians.</note> and has turned the Spirit of God—which has nonetheless often shown itself in man through wonders and great deeds—into an envious malice, as if He loved one people more than another; as if He wanted one race and not the other, so that he (the Devil, called both Christ and Satan <note>Böhme suggests the Antichrist masquerades as Christ while acting with the spirit of Satan.</note>) might sit in honor and worldly pleasures. He has stirred up war among the nations, so that the peoples have become divided and have fallen into conflicting opinions, and have provoked God to anger; for they have departed from God through these opinions. Thus, wrath has ruled over them and often destroyed them; for where there is no good, God will no longer tolerate it in His land, but gives it over to <term>wrath</term><note>original: "Zorn." In Böhme's system, "Wrath" is the "Dark Fire" or the stern quality of God's nature when separated from His "Light" or Love.</note>, even though they themselves run into it and sharpen the sword, so that one people has devoured the other.

13. Since the beginning of the world, all strife and war, as well as envy and hatred, have arisen from the Antichrist, who wants to be honored as a god in an angelic form, while the devil lurks within him. You see this same Antichrist already in Cain and Abel: how Cain [slew] his brother—

...[true] <term>Faith</term><note>original: *Glaube*. 18. A pejorative term used by Böhme to criticize the professional clergy of his day who he believed were more interested in power than piety.</note> sought only honor, greed, and pleasure within it, and led people away from God merely into their own works; thus the Suppositions became entirely blind, for they themselves went out from God into the works of their own hands, into invented ways. Therefore God also let them go, because they would not allow His Spirit to draw them. Although they have indeed been blind regarding the Kingdom of Christ, nevertheless their mind has remained in the one God, and they in harmony, where people have not reviled and blasphemed one another so hatefully for the sake of the precious Name of Christ, as those have done who have been led blindly in the darkness of their works. # Of the Threefold Life. Ch. 12.

...[-hood]<note>original: *-chen*. This is the suffix of a word from the previous page, likely *Pfaffenschafft* (priesthood) or *Geistlichkeit* (clergy).</note>, but they themselves in their <term>Opinions</term><note>original: *Meynungen*. For Böhme, this refers to sectarian dogmas and human-made beliefs that distract from a direct, living relationship with God.</note> have bitten and slandered one another like a dog over a bone, and have led the <term>Laity</term><note>The common people, distinguished from the professional clergy.</note> astray, who go groping in the dark and do not know which opinion is best: Thus you cling to opinion, and are perjured to God.

19. When the simple person is to die, he does not know where he should commit his soul; he clings to his works and to the opinion, and forsakes the will of God, and thus remains outside of God. Where do you think, then, that the poor soul remains, when it is outside of God's will? See, we wish to say this, for we know it for certain; for the Spirit of our Mother<note>Likely referring to Divine Wisdom (Sophia) or the "Eternal Nature" which Böhme often characterizes as a maternal, generative force.</note> opens this to us, so that we see it, as it were, with both hands<note>A German idiom meaning to see something with absolute, tangible clarity.</note>.

20. See, Christ says: *Where your treasure is, there is your heart also*: <note>original: "Wo ewer Schatz ist / da ist auch ewer Hertze" (Matthew 6:21).</note> See, the soul is wrapped in its opinion, and thus runs with it to the <term>Patron</term><note>In this context, the sectarian leader, saint, or theologian whose specific doctrines the soul trusted more than God’s direct will.</note> who taught it so, and seeks him out; and if it does not find him, it becomes sorrowful and has no rest, hovering thus between heaven and hell, and would gladly escape the Devil. Therefore it has come to pass that often poor souls have appeared again in the community, or else in houses, in fields, or in churches, and have called upon the community for help with their prayers, and have entered into religious <term>Orders</term><note>Monastic communities or spiritual ranks.</note>, thinking thus to receive some relief; from this, <term>Purgatory</term><note>original: *Fegfewer*. Böhme reinterprets this Catholic doctrine as a psychological and spiritual state where the soul is trapped by its own earthly attachments and false beliefs.</note> was invented. For the soul is rightly in Purgatory if it cannot reach God's will; and in such fervent immersion in opinions, it has sunk through the opinion, and yet into the still <term>Eternity</term>

<summary>Böhme argues that sectarian dogmas ("opinions") lead the soul astray, leaving it wandering after death in a state of unrest that humans have mistakenly termed Purgatory. For whatever the soul does here in this time, in which it entangles itself and which it takes into its will, that same thing it carries with it in its will, and it cannot be rid of it after the change of the body; for afterwards it has nothing else but that very thing. And even if it enters into that same thing and ignites it, and seeks diligently, it is only an unfolding of that same essence, and the poor soul must therefore be satisfied with it. Only during the time of the body can it break apart a thing that it has wrapped into its will; afterward, it stands as a broken wheel, which is shattered and of no use, and no soul enters it anymore, nor seeks anything further within it.

<margin>21.</margin> Thus we tell you, that the Antichristian souls, after the breaking of the body, do not seek the door of Christ, for they know nothing of it; they know only of that which they have grasped here. <summary>Böhme argues that the soul carries its earthly obsessions and sectarian dogmas into the afterlife, where they become a fixed reality. ## A Gate.

->The way through this world into God’s Kingdom, and how one should walk it.<-

28. You must depart from your reason <term>reason; original: *Vernunfft*</term> <note>In Böhme’s writing, "Reason" refers to the earthly, logical mind that tries to understand God through human cleverness rather than spiritual surrender.</note> and from the fleshly spirit, and lead your hearts, senses, and minds entirely into obedience to God. You must surrender your will to God’s will and not devise any ways of your own through reason, nor ask, "Where is Christ?" Direct your way in Christ and know for certain that he is in your heart. Surrender yourselves to him in great humility; cast all your deeds and intentions into his will and pleasure. Think of nothing else but that you stand at all times and hours before the clear face of God, and that Christ sits in you upon the rainbow <note>The "rainbow" is a recurring symbol in Böhme’s work, representing the bridge between the eternal and temporal worlds and the sign of God's covenant and mercy.</note> at the right hand of God. Consider that you stand every moment before the Holy Trinity <term>Trinity; original: *Dreyzahl*</term>; that God, the Holy Trinity, always examines and sees the abyss <term>abyss; original: *Abgrund*</term> <note>The *Abgrund* (Unground or Abyss) is Böhme’s term for the absolute, hidden depth of the divine or the human soul before it takes form.</note> of your heart. Think also that you do not wish to enter into any deep contemplation or searching except only into his love and mercy; and think that you never wish to depart from it, but to remain within it eternally.

29. And then, secondly, consider that you do the highest pleasure to God when you seek your brothers and sisters in this world—whoever they may be, and of whatever name or opinion <note>Böhme here promotes a spirit of tolerance, suggesting that true Christian love transcends denominational "names" or sectarian "opinions."</note> they are—with your love, and enclose them in your hearts,

Spirit and life: we receive the entire **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyzahl"</note>. The essence contains **Sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur"</note>—understand this as the body of Christ / that is the Father; Sulfur is the Father’s property. 15. Therefore, understand us correctly: In the **Lord’s Supper** <note>original: "Abendmal"</note>, we do not receive another creature with a new soul. No, but rather Christ's body—which fills the heavens—unto our soul, which was already an eternal creature. The soul eats Christ’s flesh and drinks his blood, which fills the heavens; and from that which the soul accepts and eats, it grows into a body. In that same body, it is in God’s hand and can, at the end of the world, pass through the fire of God’s wrath with that body without feeling it. Just as that same fire cannot seize Christ in the Trinity, so it cannot seize us; for the fire receives **gentleness** <note>original: "Sanfftmuth"</note> from God’s gentleness and ours, and is transformed within us into the rising desire of love, so that our fire and burning within us is a pure desire for love; for it becomes a radiance of Majesty, and thus we are in God and God’s children. The "one" represents the divine unity or "monad" which is whole and indivisible.</note> is indestructible, for it is only one and nothing more: There is nothing within it to break it, for no thing that is only one opposes itself. For when there are two wills, there is **separation**, for one often wants to go inward, and the other outward; and if the thing then has one body, the **governance** <note>original: "Regiment"; the inner ruling principle or law that directs the functions of a living being</note> in that same body is at odds. # Chapter 14. Of Man.

...captured by the devil; but if it [turns] inward into God, then the devil strikes out at it, for it is now in his territory: But when it receives Christ’s **flesh** to form a new body, it is no longer in his territory. That is a tree to him that is his **poison and death**, toward which he is hostile, and he does not like to touch it; but he incites his servants against the outer body, which must bear shame and mockery, so that he may indeed cover this tree, so that it might not be recognized; otherwise it might produce more little branches <note>In Böhme’s botanical metaphors, the "little branch" often represents a new sprout of faith or the growth of an individual soul within the community of believers.</note>, and in the end, hell might well become too narrow for him; therefore he resists while he can. Now when the poor soul breaks away from him, and turns with her dear bridegroom Christ toward God’s love, so that she enters into God’s will through **earnest repentance** and turning toward God, he still has seven **snares** <note>original: "Fallstricke." These represent the obstacles or temptations the devil uses to prevent the soul's ascent.</note>, by which he holds her with each one before he lets her go: there she must wind herself free through all seven, and leave him his ropes entirely: For the eighth, she must go through the fire; there is the <term>earnest trial</term> <note>original: "ernste Proba." In Böhme's thought, the soul must undergo a refining fire of purification to burn away earthly desires.</note>, and when she comes through there, she attains the **Heavenly Tincture** <note>original: "Himlische Tinctur." An alchemical term used here to describe the refined, divine essence or "spiritual medicine" that restores the soul's health.</note> in the **ninth number**, and in the **tenth number** upon the cross she attains Christ’s body, so that she is an angel in heaven, and a spirit on earth in this <term>valley of tabernacles</term> <note>original: "Hütten Thal." A biblical metaphor (referring to the Feast of Tabernacles or temporary dwellings) for the temporary, earthly existence of the physical body.</note>.

# Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 14.

...angel has been: Then the devil comes with his **register** <note>original: "Register." This refers to a ledger or list of the soul’s sins, which the devil uses as a legal claim in the spiritual court.</note> and reads to her what she is, and presents his justice over her: Then it is said: Bow down, and grasp the **wounds** and the **suffering of Christ**: Here it is necessary that the poor sinner takes the merit and the death of Christ and wraps himself firmly therein, for from this swaddling cloth the devil cannot tear the soul; he does not even dare to touch it, and at this place the devil must leave the soul; for Christ stands in the Father’s **wrath-fire** and is the fulfillment of obedience. There the soul is led into the **Ninth Form** <note>In Böhme’s complex cosmology, the "Ninth Form" represents a stage of high spiritual attainment beyond the seven basic properties of nature, often associated with the "Tincture" or the heavenly world.</note>, into the <term>Tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur." An alchemical term used by Böhme to describe a spiritual essence or "dye" that transforms base nature into divine light.</note> of eternal life; there she is embraced by God’s Majesty, and the beautiful, gracious **Virgin of the Wisdom of God** meets her with her pearl-wreath, and crowns the soul as a **Knight of Heaven**. What joy there is here for God’s angels, and what joy the soul attains there, we have no pen to write, nor do we have any mouth in this world to speak such things. We only wish for the reader and all people that they might experience it themselves—for which cause we go about this writing with much effort and deep labor—for we write what we ourselves have recognized and seen with **spiritual eyes**: We do not say this for our own glory, but so that the reader may know, if he wishes to follow us, what he has to expect; since he otherwise sees that the world regards God's children only as an **owl** <note>original: "Eule." A contemporary idiom: just as an owl is mocked and chased by other birds when it appears in daylight, the spiritual person is mocked by the worldly who do not understand their "light."</note>; but we shall well delight ourselves in this after this short life: So this is also to us...

He oppresses the simple with harsh words, takes his sweat, and plagues him in his body. 13. When **Reason** <note>original: *Vernunfft*; in Böhme’s writing, "Reason" often refers to the natural, earth-bound intellect that lacks spiritual illumination and relies only on worldly logic.</note> looks around and considers, it says: "I see nothing that is different from ancient times. Furthermore, the world has always been both evil and good, as the histories show. Also, one must strive and act in this way, otherwise one would surely have to be the world's **fool and owl** <note>original: *Narr und Eule*; a proverbial expression meaning someone who is mocked and shunned by society.</note>; indeed, one would surely die of hunger. If I did not leave room for my children to learn the customs and **luxury** <note>original: *Uppigkeit*; implies not just wealth, but excess and worldly vanity.</note> of the world, they would surely be despised. And if I do not also present myself with pomp and pride, I am considered nothing. But if I am to have these things, I must surely use **cunning**; I will likely attain nothing with truth, love, and justice. I must only do as other people do, so that I can also live alongside others. Should I then be the world’s fool all alone? Even if I sin, God is nonetheless gracious and merciful. Has not Christ strangled sin and death on the **Cross**, and taken away the Devil’s power? You can still surely repent and be saved." This is the **rule of the world** <note>original: *Welt Regul*; the standard operating procedure or logic by which society functions.</note>; this is what the high and the low practice, the shepherd with the sheep. The suffering of Christ must be the **cover for wickedness** <note>original: *Schalckheit Deckel*; the idea that people use the doctrine of Grace as a legalistic "cover-up" to continue living immorally.</note>. Everyone wants to be a Christian under Christ’s cover, even while the poor soul sits as a harlot for the Devil. As long as the mouth confesses itself a Christian and covers its wickedness with Christ’s **purple mantle** <note>original: *Purpur-Mantel*; a reference to the robe placed on Jesus during his Passion, here used metaphorically as a garment of false righteousness.</note>, then all is well. We are thus indeed magnificent **mouth-Christians** <note>original: *Maul-Christen*; those who are Christians in name or speech only, but not in heart or deed.</note> under Christ’s cover, while in our hearts we have the **Antichristian harlot** residing as a guest.

### Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 19.
<meta>catchword: or</meta>

The soul presses with its repentant will out of the <term>Center of Anguish</term> <note>Boehme’s "Centrum der Angst" refers to the core of natural existence characterized by restless desire and self-centeredness.</note> / out of the abyss of hell / and also out of the spirit of this world, into the <term>second Principle</term> in God / which is also in the soul / for all three <term>Principles</term> <note>Boehme’s system of Three Principles: 1. The dark/fire world (source of power), 2. The light/love world (divine), 3. The outer world of nature.</note> are in the soul / namely two eternal ones / and then the fragile one / which brings about the death of this world.

-> Thus understand us dearly: <-

9. God the Father does not move himself / only the Holy Spirit moves / although that alone would not help us : Only the Word <note>original: "das Wort"; referring to Christ as the divine Logos.</note> / which created our soul / has become human / it has the Holy Spirit within it / and the Spirit proceeds from the Father within the Word / and meets the calling mind and will / and opens itself from the inside out within the soul / for the outer animal body is not worthy of the Holy Spirit opening himself within it / though it does happen at times with the Saints / that he goes out from the soul into the outer principle / where the body triumphs / and knows not what is happening to it for joy. But in the soul's new body in Christ / when she receives Christ’s body / there the Holy Spirit dwells within: And when the Devil then comes / and wishes to tempt the soul from below in the <term>first Principle</term> <note>original: "primo Principio"</note> / in the <term>Center of the first four forms</term> <note>The "four forms" of the dark world are the foundational qualities of nature: contraction, expansion, rotation, and fire.</note> toward the torment of fire / then the will of the soul presses into the flesh of Christ / into the <term>second Principle</term> <note>original: "ander Principium"</note> within itself / there she is softened and redeemed / and the Devil must go down : For that life does not taste good to him : Yet he is so defiant / and watches the soul / as often as he sees that she is secure [complacent] /

<summary>Boehme explains how the soul moves from the "Center of Anguish" into the divine light of the Second Principle through the indwelling of the Holy Spirit and Christ's Word. He describes the spiritual warfare occurring between the new "body in Christ" and the Devil’s attempts to pull the soul back into the fiery first principle of nature.</summary>

God does not dwell in the external, for the external is the animal <term>astral spirit</term> <note>original: "Thierische Stern-Geist"; this refers to the lower psychological and physical nature of man, influenced by the stars and worldly desires, rather than the divine center.</note>. He dwells within himself, in the interior: The external <term>being</term> <note>original: "Wesen"; the outward substance or manifestation of reality.</note> is only a figure and likeness of God. It is indeed God's, and born out of the inner <term>center</term> <note>original: "Centro"; the foundational point of spiritual manifestation.</note>, spoken through the <insert>Word of creation</insert> <note>original: "Verbum fiat"; Latin for "Let it be done," the creative Word of God from Genesis.</note>, but it is not the essence of the <term>Trinity</term> <note>original: "Dreyzahl"; literally "the Three-Number," referring to the Triune nature of God.</note>, which is one being and spirit in a trinity, above nature, and yet dwells in nature within itself, incomprehensible to nature, just as the wind and the light are not seized by the fire, and yet are the fire’s spirit, radiance, and life.

### Chapter 16. Of Man.

Of Nature <note>original Latin: "Naturæ"</note>, and is something other than the Center, yet the Center brings it forth nonetheless; and it hovers in all omnipotence over the Center, and rules over it, just as God rules over nature; and yet the name of the Trinity <note>original: "Dreyzahl," literally "Three-number," Böhme's term for the Holy Trinity</note> has its origin in eternal nature: And just as God is free from nature, and yet nature is of His being <note>original: "Wesen," implying essence or substance</note>, and is inseparable from God: So also the soul; it is free from nature and is a lord of nature, for it is one spirit with God, and yet it blooms or grows out of nature: Indeed, God is not to be completely compared with the soul, for God's eternal will is only the cause and beginning of nature; but with God's Majesty, whose radiance arises out of the sharpness of eternal nature, and yet originates before nature as the flash of eternal freedom, from which nature, in its sharp birthing <note>original: "Gebährung," the generative process of reality</note>, catches the radiance, and raises it in the fire to a triumphant high light: For which cause eternal freedom longs to be outside of nature, that it may be manifest in wonders, and have majesty and glory and power: For if there were no nature, there would also be no glory and power, much less majesty, and also no spirit, but rather a silence without being.

revelation of Being <note>original: "Wesens Offenbarung." Böhme uses "Being" or "Essence" to describe the underlying reality of God.</note>. <meta>This page continues the discussion from page 439, where Jacob Böhme explains the relationship between the eternal "Being" (Wesen) and the human soul. # Of the Threefold Life, Ch. 16

revelation of Being <note>original: "Wesens Offenbarung." Böhme uses "Being" or "Essence" to describe the underlying reality of God and the source of all existence.</note>. So then, since the soul—as a spirit—has been opened and taken from this Being, it also has two forms: One is *Nature* <note>original Latin: "Natura"</note>, and the other is the **Divine Flower**, or the growth out of nature, which is above nature, and is a spirit in itself, just as God is a spirit in Himself. You can see an example of this in fire: Fire belongs to nature; but the radiance along with the air that rises from the fire is a spirit possessing all the power of the fire’s nature, yet it is above the fire’s nature, for the fire's nature cannot grasp it. Furthermore, the fire's nature could not persist if the spirit of the air did not blow upon the fire again. Thus, the fire gives birth to the spirit with the **radiance**, and longs intensely for that spirit again, drawing it back into itself constantly, yet it cannot hold it. For that spirit is the fire's life, and the radiance comes out of the sharpness <term>Sharpness (Schärffe): Böhme's term for the harsh, contractive, and painful quality of the first principles of nature.</term> of the fire, and yet there is no feeling <note>original: "Fühlung," implying the painful sensation of burning or heat.</note> in the radiance; and the radiance possesses the power, not the fire. For from the power of the radiance, life arises and a plant grows, but not from the fire—as you may see this in the radiance of the sun.

## Concerning the Amen of the Conclusion.

A is the first letter, and it pushes out from the heart; it has no nature <term>nature: In Böhme's terminology, "nature" refers to the realm of manifestation, conflict, and desire; that which is "outside nature" is the pure, undifferentiated Will of God.</term>, but rather we clearly perceive within it the longing <note>original: "Sucht." While often meaning "sickness" today, Böhme uses it to mean a driving, passionate craving or searching.</note> of the eternal Will outside of nature, in which nature is brought forth, and which has been from eternity. For the Will desires the Heart, and the Heart desires the Will: It is Father and Son, and the power that proceeds from them is the Spirit of eternal life, of which we have spoken previously.

27. Now, since the A is born out of the heart, as if from the eternal Will, and thrusts out from the Will, then the entire alphabet with twenty-four numbers follows from the A. For the A begins to count, and encompasses the whole number with the *men* <note>Böhme is breaking down the word "A-men." The "A" is the beginning/source, and "men" is the fulfillment or the gathering of all things.</note>. These are the wonders and works of God which appear in the Spirit beyond nature, as in the luster of Majesty.

28. Understand it in this way: We are with our souls in a foreign inn, namely in the spirit of this world, which holds the soul captive within itself. We could not, therefore, come into God if God had not become Man, who has led our soul into the Word—into the living power of God—within Himself. Now we are branches on that same tree, and we must draw the sap of the tree into ourselves if we wish to grow green from the tree. Otherwise, if we only imagine <note>original: "imaginiren." For Böhme, "imagination" is a creative, formative power where the soul's desire "images" or "shapes" its reality.</note> toward the air and the sun, our branch withers. Our will must be directed into the tree, and that is prayer. When we pray, the will goes...

# Of the Threefold Life Chap. 17.

## The XVII. Chapter.
### Of the Blessing of God in this World; a very good revelation for the person of weak faith.

1 Dear children, if we turn back from our **reason** <term>Vernunfft: Böhme frequently uses this term to describe human intellect or "school-learning" which, when separated from the Spirit, remains blind to divine truths.</term> and surrender ourselves to the **Will of God**, so that He may create and do with us what He will: when we put our trust in Him, we enter into our **True Father**, and are His children. Just as a father cares for his children, so also does God our Father care for us, as Christ faithfully teaches us: *Seek first the Kingdom of God, and His righteousness, and all these other things shall be added unto you.* Also: *Behold the birds under the heavens; they neither sow nor spin, nor do they gather into barns, yet your Heavenly Father feeds them: are you not much better than they, O you of little faith!* <note>Böhme is paraphrasing the Sermon on the Mount from Matthew 6; he uses these verses to emphasize that spiritual alignment brings about material providence.</note>

It always thinks its sins are too many, that it cannot reach the Majesty of God. In Böhme's cosmology, "Wrath" is the dark, consuming fire of the first principle, which the Devil tries to draw the soul into.</note> and pulls the smoke into the soul's will, so that it stays behind, fearing God. # Of the Threefold Life, Chapter 16.

...the shepherds, as well as the prophets and apostles; then you will soon see whom God chooses: whether He chooses human art or the Spirit <note>original: "Kunst oder Geist." Böhme consistently contrasts "Kunst" (academic, external, or man-made learning) with the "Geist" (the direct, internal inspiration of the Holy Spirit).</note>.

16. Therefore, let everyone take heed of their station <term>station: "Standt," referring to one's social position, profession, or "calling" in the world</term> in which they reside. One who works therein, works God’s wonders; he enters with his will into God’s will in simplicity, and clings to God in a childlike manner. He follows only two paths: one into his work, by which he provides nourishment for the body <note>original: "dem Bauch Nahrung" (food for the belly).</note>; the other into God’s will, trusting God in whatever He may do or make of him. And wherever he is, and whatever he does, he says: "It is my calling; Lord, Your will be done; give me what is good for me." Such a person walks rightly in God’s wondrous works.

17. But he who is chosen by nature to be a ruler and a leader—especially in the spiritual estate <term>spiritual estate: "Geistlichen Stande," the clergy or those in religious leadership</term>—should well take heed of his affairs, so that he does not go without weapons; for he leads Christ’s flock. He is a shepherd, and the wolf is always prowling around him. If he is vigilant and recognizes that he has Christ’s sheep under his pasture, and grazes them rightly as a faithful shepherd, then the shepherd’s staff will be a great glory to him in eternity. But if he seeks only the wool—his own honor, power, pomp, and magnificence, his own pleasure—and squanders the wool of the sheep, neither feeding nor watering them, but instead snores like a sluggard in the lusts of the flesh, so that one sheep goes here and another there, wandering astray and being devoured by the wolf—he who does not want to enter the sheepfold, but stands outside...

<summary>Böhme explains that God chooses the simple of heart over the academically learned, urging individuals to find God within their daily labor and warning religious leaders of their duty to protect their flock from spiritual neglect.</summary>
<keywords>vocation, Holy Spirit, simplicity, shepherds, spiritual leadership, greed, divine will, Christ's flock</keywords>

# Chapter 18. Of Man.

...prowls around, and watches how he may steal the sheep’s fodder with cunning and shear their wool. All these belong among the wolves; they do not hold Christ’s shepherd’s staff, but rather the **Devil’s razor** <note>original: "Teuffels Scheermesser." Böhme uses this sharp metaphor to describe greedy clergy who "fleece" their congregation rather than feeding them.</note>, and they must hereafter howl eternally with the wolves.

18. How can anyone call himself a shepherd of Christ if he has not been chosen for that role by the Spirit of Christ? Can a wolf appoint a shepherd over the sheep? Are they not both wolves? Or do we say this out of mere impulse? It is a fact of nature that an evil thing cannot produce a good thing from itself, but only another evil thing. How then can one angry soldier make another angry man kind, when his only intent is to murder and strike? Or how do you expect to awaken the **Holy Spirit** in man when your own voice contains only the spirit of this world? That will certainly not happen, unless the Spirit was already awakened in the listener beforehand. Such a listener hears the voice of the Holy Spirit in every word spoken regarding the wonders of God. And if a donkey could speak <note>A reference to the biblical story of Balaam’s donkey (Numbers 22), where God used an animal to speak truth to a prophet.</note> and spoke of God’s word, the **hammer of awakening** would strike the soul that is rooted in God. For Christ says: *He who is of God hears God’s words; the reason you do not hear them is that you are not of God*, but are of the devil and the spirit of this world.

19. In many a person there is no Word of God or Spirit to be awakened at all, because the **fierce matrix** <term>fierce matrix: "grimme Matrix." In Böhme's philosophy, the "Matrix" is the creative womb of nature. The "fierce" or "wrathful" quality refers to the dark, foundational fire of existence that has not been softened by divine light or love.</term> has imprisoned them. This is demonstrated by the way Christ spoke; He certainly possessed the hammer <note>The "hammer" is a recurring Böhme metaphor for the divine Word or vibration that strikes the "sound" or "spirit" out of the human soul.</note>; yet His Spirit did not go...

<summary>Böhme argues that spiritual leadership requires divine election by the Holy Spirit rather than human appointment, warning that a "spiritless" teacher cannot awaken the soul of a listener. He emphasizes that a soul truly rooted in God will recognize the divine Word even from the lowliest source.</summary>

...into the malicious, hardened soul, but into these who would gladly be pious, if they only could. And when the **hammer** <note>Böhme uses the "hammer" as a metaphor for the Word of God or the Holy Spirit striking the "anvil" of the soul to wake it up.</note> then awakens the soul-spirit, so that the soul turns around and throws itself into God, then it is able to do so. The **old man** <note>A biblical reference to the sinful, unregenerate nature of humanity.</note> must not have the dominion, but rather **God's Spirit**; otherwise, there is no "ability" there, but only a clinging to **Wrath**. For there are two cravings <note>original: "Sucht." While this word means "addiction" or "sickness" in modern German, Böhme uses it to describe a fundamental, driving passion or intense longing that directs the soul’s energy.</note> in the soul: one is the greedy, fierce **fire-craving**, which always seeks the earthly essence; and then there is one from the spirit which is born out of the fire, wherein we understand the true soul-life in the **image of God**. This is **God’s craving**, and it seeks the Kingdom of Heaven.

Now, if the right hammer—the Spirit of God—strikes therein, then that same craving becomes so strong that it overcomes the **fire-source** <note>original: "Feuer-Quall." This term refers to the agonizing, vibrating source of energy in Böhme’s cosmology.</note> and craving, and softens it, so that it desires the "dear craving"—the craving of the soul-spirit. There, good can be done. Such a soul is easily awakened so that it may subdue the outer dominion; and especially when the right hammer of the **Holy Spirit** sounds through the ears into the heart, then the **soul’s tincture** <term>tincture: an alchemical term for a spiritual essence or "medicine" that has the power to transform and penetrate everything it touches</term> quickly catches fire. From there, it goes through the entire soul-spirit and out through both cravings, for it throws itself into a single will. For **two wills** cannot consist in eternity; there must only be one. The one must be as if powerless, and the other **Almighty**, otherwise there is discord.

20. For that is the law of eternity and eternal persistence: that it has only **one will**. If it had two, one would break the other, and there would be strife. It looks indeed into many powers and...

# Of the Threefold Life Chap. 18.

is of the same <term>essences <note>original: "Essentien." In Böhme's cosmology, these are the fundamental spiritual substances or qualities that constitute the inner nature of a being.</note></term>; but whoever does not have these essences does not desire it for food, nor does he gather it.

22. Therefore, let every soul reflect and test itself, what kind of fruit it may be: Here [in this life] it is still possible to turn back, and to hew down the weed, and to bring forth a better plant from the root; but when the Great Reaper <note>original: "Einerndter." A reference to God or the Angel of Judgment who harvests the world at the end of time.</note> comes, he will cut them all down together, and then the weeds will be bound into bundles and cast into the fire; but the good plant shall be carried to God’s table.

23. This we have revealed very faithfully according to our gifts: and whoever hungers, let him eat, and whoever thirsts, let him drink: It is to be taken without money <note>A reference to the biblical promise in Isaiah 55:1, suggesting that spiritual truth and grace are given freely to those who seek them.</note>, so that our joy in God may be full, and that we may also have food to eat in that other life. Hallelujah, Amen.
